title: The Shorter Line
blurb: Make this line shorter, says Akbar. And do not touch it.
script:
[warmly] One bright morning in Delhi… Emperor Akbar was feeling playful. [amused] He walked into his court with a piece of chalk in his hand, and every minister stood up very straight, because a playful emperor is the most dangerous kind.

[grandly] He went to the wall. And slowly… carefully… he drew a long white line. [short pause] From here… all the way… to there.

[curious] The ministers looked at the line. The line looked back at them. [gently] Nobody said anything at all.

[grandly] “Now,” said Akbar, turning round with a smile, “I want one of you to make this line SHORTER.” [short pause] “But you may not touch it. You may not rub it. You may not wash it away. [slyly] Not one finger on my line.”

[worried] Oh, the court did not like that.

[whispers] One minister said the line could be covered with a cloth. [firmly] “That is hiding it,” said Akbar. “Not shortening it.”

[whispers] Another said they might scrape the wall. [firmly] “That is touching it,” said Akbar.

[thoughtful] A third minister said nothing at all, and studied his own shoes very carefully… which is what ministers do when they have run out of ideas.

[calmly] And in the corner, Birbal was smiling. [gently] Not a big smile. Just the small one he wore when he had already thought of the answer and was being polite about it.

[excited] “Birbal!” called the Emperor. “You are smiling. That means you know.”

[cheerfully] “I might, Your Majesty,” said Birbal. “May I borrow the chalk?”

[curious] Birbal walked up to the wall. The whole court leaned forward. [short pause] He did not rub the line. He did not wash the line. He did not touch the line at all.

[calmly] He simply drew a SECOND line… right underneath it… [slowly] longer… and longer… and longer… all the way to the end of the wall.

[surprised] And then he stepped back and folded his hands.

[thoughtful] Emperor Akbar stared at the two lines.

[softly] The first line had not changed at all. Not one grain of chalk had moved. [amused] And yet… beside that great long line beneath it… it looked SMALL. It looked short. It looked like a little scratch on the wall.

[laughs heartily] “It IS shorter!” said Akbar. “It is shorter and I watched you not touch it!”

[warmly] “Nothing was taken away, Your Majesty,” said Birbal. “Something was only… put beside it.”

[gently] “A thing looks big or small depending on what stands next to it. [softly] Your line did not change. Only what it stood beside.”

[short pause] [amused] Akbar looked at the wall for a long, long time. Then he laughed, and left both lines exactly where they were.

[softly] And for years afterwards, visitors to the palace would see two chalk lines on a wall, and wonder why an emperor had never washed them off. [long pause] [whispers] Now… you know.
